channel.title: AAE Updates
channel.description: Updates for AAE, the Accessible Android Emulator.

item.title: Version 0.6.0
item.description: • Googlebook devices, on Macs with Apple silicon: Googlebook OS (Android 17, desktop) in a QEMU virtual machine. New Device, "Googlebook OS (Android 17), virtual machine". First use downloads about 9 GB; the disk takes about 20 GB.

item.title: Version 0.5.1
item.description:
• Keyboard layouts for 52 languages. The device follows the computer's keyboard; on a Mac, typed characters are sent as typed, so layouts such as British are right.
  • Cold Boot, in the Device menu: starts without the saved state.
  • Foldable devices, with Fold and Unfold.
  • Gesture mode: W gives the pixel position, D reads the properties of the element at the touch point.
  • Fixes: Windows crashed when saving Settings; a device that shut down on an empty battery wouldn't start; a device locked after a cold boot; slow fallback to software graphics on some graphics adapters.

item.title: Version 0.5.0
item.description:
• Speech bridge: the device's screen reader speech goes to the host's text-to-speech instead of as audio. Mac: VoiceOver's or Spoken Content's voice and rate. Windows: NVDA 2024.1 or later, otherwise SAPI 5. AAE Remote: the phone's text-to-speech.
  • Microphone: the computer's or phone's microphone into the device while an app records, a microphone check, and Play Audio File into Microphone.
  • Display and Language: language, font and display size, dark theme, bold and high contrast text, colour inversion and correction, animations, captions, and settings for new devices.
  • Network controls, battery health, fingerprint touches, shake, GPX routes, and Power, Assistant and volume buttons.
  • Record Screen, with audio. Accessibility Inspector follows the screen and saves as HTML.
  • Hardware settings, device export and import, audio output per device, and a choice of return-to-host shortcut.
  • Apps reconnect to a device restarted by another AAE process. Turning the speech log on or off no longer restarts the screen reader.

item.title: Version 0.4.0
item.description:
• AAE Remote, a new Android app, uses this computer's devices from your phone: their sound and vibrations play on the phone, and you manage and use them with keyboard and gesture modes and the testing tools. Turn on File, Serve Devices to Phones, then pair your phone with the code AAE shows.
  • AAE can serve devices whenever you log in, without being open.
  • Quitting while a device is stopping now waits for it, so its emulator isn't left running.
  • Speak Status names the screen reader, and an app made only for ARM processors gets a clear message when it can't install.

item.title: Version 0.3.1
item.description:
• Devices are much faster: they now draw their screens with the computer's graphics adapter. Before, the emulator drew them in software, on the processor.
  • Speech no longer fails on a device's first start when the speech engine is slow to answer.
  • AAE says when a computer is below what it needs, and gives devices fewer processor cores on small processors.
  • Diagnostic reports name the processor and graphics, and keep more personal details out.

item.title: Version 0.3.0
item.description: • AAE 0.3.0 is the first version with a stable Windows app. Nothing has changed in the Mac app; it has the same version number as the Windows app.

item.title: Version 0.2.2
item.description:
AAE 0.2.2

  • Android 17, and Android 16's later update (API 36.1), can now be downloaded. AAE couldn't read the way Google numbers them.
  • New Device can include previews of upcoming Android releases: turn on Include Previews.
  • Fixed: setting up an Android 15 device stopped at "Setting up the full keyboard", with an error ending in "Killed".

item.title: Version 0.2.1
item.description:
AAE 0.2.1

  • Fixed: downloading Backtalk failed with "it isn't signed with Backtalk's key" on Macs without Java. AAE now checks Backtalk itself, with no Java needed.
  • Fixed: if Android dropped AAE's full keyboard while a device was running, Meta and the Home button stopped working. AAE now selects it again whenever it connects to a device.
  • Apps (Option-Command-P): open, stop, clear or uninstall a device's apps, and grant their permissions and special access.
  • Accessibility Services (Option-Command-U): turn any accessibility service on or off, and switch screen readers in one step.
  • Open Link (Command-Shift-L) and Send Intent, and Watch for New Builds, which installs each new build of an app as it's made.
  • AI agents can now run and test devices through AAE's MCP server, including hearing what the screen reader says.

item.title: Version 0.2.0
item.description:
AAE 0.2.0

  • Several devices at once: Open in Own Window (Option-Command-O) gives a device a window of its own, with its own keyboard focus. With several devices running, AAE plays only the one you're using; you can turn that off in Settings.
  • Each device has its own volume: a slider, and Option-Command-Up and Down.
  • Wipe a device back to how it was first set up, with its screen reader set up again.
  • Help, Run Self-Test checks everything AAE needs and reads out what it found.
  • Speech and sound arrive about 15 milliseconds sooner.

item.title: Version 0.1.0
item.description:
AAE 0.1.0

The first release of AAE, the Accessible Android Emulator: create, run and test Android virtual devices without sighted help.

  • Sets up Google's Android emulator and tools itself, and downloads Android versions, with Google's licence shown for you to accept.
  • Named devices, several of the same Android version, with a screen reader from first boot: Backtalk on Android 8 and later, or your own.
  • Your whole keyboard in Android, with Command as Meta, and system shortcuts included. Control-Command-Escape returns to the Mac.
  • Screen reader gestures from the keyboard, at any point on the screen.
  • Dependable speech and sound, with older Android's pitch corrected.
  • Testing tools: accessibility inspector and checks, speech log, device log and shell.
  • Apps, snapshots, clipboard, battery, location, messages and calls.

For Macs with Apple silicon, on macOS 13 or later.
